policies.title: Grenada: named ordinary passports exempt from visitor visa
policies.summary: Grenada's active Embassy-linked citizenship schedule directly marks these passport issuers No Visa required.
conditions: Applies to ordinary passport holders travelling as short visitors under the nationality category directly named in Grenada's schedule.
Argentina is explicitly limited by the schedule to a 30-day visitor stay; no duration is inferred for the other named passport codes.

The schedule's no-visa label concerns entry-visa requirements only. Work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment remain outside this finding.
The actively linked PDF has inconsistent cover and page-level update marks and should be rechecked before promotion or travel reliance.

policies.title: Grenada: named ordinary passports require visitor visa before travel
policies.summary: Grenada's active Embassy-linked citizenship schedule directly places these passport issuers in its Prior to Arrival category, defined as a mission or consulate visa before travel.
conditions: Applies to ordinary passport holders travelling as short visitors under the nationality category directly named in Grenada's schedule.
The schedule defines Prior to Arrival as a visa obtained at a Grenada mission or consulate before travel; it is not an eVisa or arrival-issued visa.
Purpose-specific, work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment remain outside this finding.
The actively linked PDF has inconsistent cover and page-level update marks and should be rechecked before promotion or travel reliance.

policies.title: Grenada: named ordinary passports receive visitor visa at port of entry after pre-clearance
policies.summary: Grenada's active Embassy-linked citizenship schedule places Belarus and Kazakhstan in its Port of Entry category; the linked instructions require pre-clearance before travel, followed by visa issuance on arrival in Grenada.
conditions: Applies to an ordinary Belarusian or Kazakh passport holder travelling as a short visitor under the nationality category directly named in Grenada's schedule.
The schedule defines Port of Entry as a visa granted on arrival in Grenada, not an electronic approval or a visa-free admission.

Before travel, apply for a Grenada Immigration and Passport Office pre-clearance letter; the live instructions recommend applying at least six weeks before departure. The visa itself is granted on arrival in Grenada.
Purpose-specific, work, study, residence, transit, diplomatic, official, service, special-document and final-admission treatment remain outside this finding.
The actively linked PDF has inconsistent cover and page-level update marks and should be rechecked before promotion or travel reliance.

conflicts.explanation: Grenada's active Embassy-linked schedule directly places Benin in Prior to Arrival, which it defines as a visa obtained at a Grenada mission or consulate before travel.
Grenada's active Embassy-linked schedule directly places Belarus in Port of Entry, which it defines as a visa granted on arrival after the linked pre-clearance process.
Grenada's active Embassy-linked schedule directly places Kazakhstan in Port of Entry, which it defines as a visa granted on arrival after the linked pre-clearance process.
